items.title: 68251_Teddy McRae oral history interview
items.q: I think I got a guy who did all the writing for Alan Freed... He did the music -- he did the writing for me.

ctx.x:
Yeah.
Anyway, what we did, Bob Rolontz -- only he had Piano Red out of Chicago. See, he had a hard time getting artists because he didn't know too much about rhythm and blues.
See, he took that job because RCA Victor wanted some of this rock and roll stuff. But they wanted to put it on RCA's label.
What they did, they created another label called Groove Records, so they brought in this rhythm and blues stuff.
So when I walked in, "Mr. Bear" "Peel-A-Bos" (inaudible) doing all this stuff with them, you know. Keep…
And they walked in and -- I think I got a guy who did all the writing for Alan Freed. What's his name -- I got him to do (inaudible), because he was doing all --
